A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWE-SQL work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original BIRD-CRITIC evaluations, BIRD-Fixer fine-tuning results, component ablations and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds trajectory-sampling comparisons, complexity-stratified results and synthetic-data analyses.

M1.justification: Table 4 adds an evaluated Reject + f-Plan collection variant combining plan guidance with up to five rejection-sampling trials. The core SQL-Rewind, SQL-ACT, f-Plan and GTM procedures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a change to the pipeline producing the main BIRD-Fixer results.

E1.justification: Both versions use 530 BIRD-CRITIC-PG tasks, 570 BIRD-CRITIC-MULTI tasks across the same four dialects, and 3,301 SIX-GYM instances. The new analyses examine retained data and complexity subsets without introducing different task requirements or environments. Preliminary file-saving workflow experiments already appear in v1's limitations.

E2.justification: The new trajectory-generation comparison evaluates rejection sampling and its combination with f-Plan alongside the existing vanilla and plan-guided collection approaches. Comparator membership in the main model evaluations and component ablations is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added sampling study specifies single-attempt rollouts at temperature 0, rejection sampling at temperature 0.8 with up to five attempts and early stopping, and comparisons of attempts, database time and cost. Table 9 introduces complexity-stratified evaluation. Existing benchmark, fine-tuning and inference settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Section 6.4 and Appendix 14.3 substantially extend validation: they test f-Plan against additional sampling, examine its advantage across SQL complexity, and compare synthetic training data with manually curated benchmark data. These address efficiency and training-data representativeness beyond v1's retained component ablations and error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experimental results average five repeated trials, without adding confidence intervals or significance tests. The new rejection-sampling attempt counts describe the generation procedure, not a change in statistical replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 4, 8 and 9 add substantial results, including 1,910 rejection-sampling trajectories, 2,560 combined trajectories, resource measurements, synthetic-data statistics and complexity-specific success rates. Main benchmark scores, original trajectory counts and component-ablation scores remain unchanged. Figure 9 also changes the second observation from one publisher row to two identical rows.

T1.justification: The task mapping, success-rate definition and formalized Algorithms 1–2 are retained. No assumptions, theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations are added; the new diversity ratio is a descriptive evaluation statistic.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark and method contributions, the 73.7% trajectory increase, and BIRD-Fixer's reported 38.11% and 29.65% success rates. Claims about SQL-debugging difficulty, open-source agents and cross-dialect generalization retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new comparisons as evidence that structured plans narrow the search space and help increasingly with SQL complexity. It also expands explanations of semantic alignment and cascading reasoning failures in the error analysis. Existing workflow and single-turn limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Table 4 documents rollout temperatures, retry limits, stopping behavior and resource costs, while Figure 10 supplies a concrete functional-plan example. Existing hardware, library versions, LoRA settings, model identifiers, prompts and access information remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds Micro-act and SHARE to the citations and bibliography, naming SHARE among methods improving smaller text-to-SQL models. The broader related-work organization and claimed novelty of SQL issue debugging remain unchanged; these citations are not newly evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v3 adds focused sampling and validation subsections, expands the error-analysis prose, adds acknowledgments and an appendix contents page, and moves the algorithm appendix after experimental details. Author/contact formatting and publication information change, but most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands with new efficiency, data-comparison and complexity tables (Tables 4, 8 and 9), plus a new diagram illustrating f-Plan's backward inference and forward validation (Figure 10). Figure 9 is revised, and existing tables, figures and algorithms are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's vanilla-rollout comparison, v3 provides useful competing-sampler, resource-cost and complexity evidence, plus information about synthetic-data representativeness. These gains outweigh localized inaccuracies: the 'similar overhead' wording needs qualification given costs of $27.44 versus $8.47, and revised Figure 9 introduces duplicate publisher rows despite GROUP BY. The net improvement is limited rather than a substantial strengthening of the whole paper.
